claim: Comet Cash is the one game played less than its neighbours in both halves of the year: 0.81x in Jan-Mar and 0.82x in Apr-Jun (75% of its 24 machines below 0.85x). That is a game-title question, not a single-machine one.

claim: Repairs, maintenance and moves do not change how machines pay out: across 1,214 tickets, no before/after shift in hit rate or hold reaches |z| >= 4, and the change scores look like pure noise (sd 1.06 and 1.02).

result: 0 of 1,214 tickets shift; floor-wide hit-rate z sd 1.01 without M-1158
alternative_tested: Multiple testing: threshold raised to |z| >= 4 because ~6 false alarms are expected at |z| >= 3
limitation: Tickets near the window edges have shorter comparison windows (min 7 days per side)

claim: Moving a machine to a stronger bank raises its play value, but by an uncertain amount: across the 3 moves to stronger banks, TPAH rose $5.58/h on average net of the floor trend, capturing about half (52%) of the predicted bank gap. The one Back Forty -> Main Entrance move more than doubled TPAH ($14.00 -> $32.14/h).
result: Realisation range -57% to +195%; effects range -$0.95 to +$17.28/h
alternative_tested: Floor-wide trend subtracted (difference-in-differences against the whole floor over the same days); move day excluded
limitation: Only 4 moves (3 to stronger banks), one with 20 days after; use as a rough scale factor for R3a, with a wide range

claim: The manager's 10 earned $554k less than a typical machine. Location explains $203k, high-payback game settings $148k, short time on the floor $133k, luck $63k (mostly M-1158), lower play volume only $7k, and downtime about $0. The machines are not unpopular; they stand in a weak spot, run games that keep little per bet, or were not on the floor long.
result: Pieces add up exactly to each machine's gap (max error $0.000000 over 310 machines)
alternative_tested: Exposure, availability, location (bank peers), play volume, game hold and luck separated in one exact identity
limitation: Typical machine = median availability and median TPAH; bank peer medians from 4-7 machines; location piece includes the walkway closure months

claim: No machine loses money with average luck: every machine's theo exceeds its supplied costs, and no leased machine's lease + service cost exceeds its theo. 8 of the manager's 10 are leased; on expected contribution per available hour they are 8 of the floor's bottom 10, still earning $3.78-$7.27/h.
result: 0 machines with negative expected contribution; 0 leased machines with lease + service > theo
alternative_tested: Expected contribution (theo) used instead of house win, so luck does not decide profitability
limitation: Supplied costs are partial (no rent, tax, depreciation, full staffing): contribution after supplied costs only

claim: The day-of-week forecast (chosen in April, tested once on May-June) misses daily coin-in by about 5%. On ordinary weekends it was off by -5.5% (normal range ±4%), so an 18% promotion lift is detectable but a 6% lift is not. It changes how success is judged: against a flat average an ordinary weekend already looks +12% better.

result: see claim
alternative_tested: Two richer candidates lost in April; weekend error measured on the 7 ordinary (no-event) weekends of May-June

claim: None of the manager's 10 is clearly weak because of the machine itself. M-1179 is borderline (play 0.78x its neighbours, close to the 0.75-0.85 band) and should be reviewed again; the rest are explained by location (the largest single cause, 37% of the $553,702 combined shortfall), the game's payback setting, short time on the floor, or a payout pattern to inspect.

claim: Fund: Comp policy pilot with control group x1 ($4,000); Machine inspection and paytable verification x1 ($1,200); Property promotion weekend x1 ($15,000); keep $79,800. claim: A machine's expected win per available hour can be estimated from its bank, game and manufacturer: fitted on January-April and tested on May-June, the estimator's average error was $0.97/h (6.0%), against $2.83/h for the bank average and $4.35/h for the floor median.

limitation: Combinations not present on the floor rely on separate game and location effects; business-level shifts are handled by the July floor forecast factor

claim: The May 1 change raised the potential cost of points members already hold: 156 million unredeemed points would cost $7,561,306 if all were redeemed at the new rate, against $3,333,427 at the old rate; at the 4.4% redemption rate seen so far, about $185,350 more.

claim: Across the floor, machines are very similar once location, game and manufacturer are allowed for: 90% earn between 0.93 and 1.05 of expectation. Only 2 of 308 consistently earn more than 10% less, in both halves: M-1184, M-1154, both Jackpot Summit in the Back Forty. Jackpot Summit runs at 0.83-0.91 of expectation in the Back Forty but 0.99-1.09 elsewhere, so the remedy is where the game stands. 17 machines are on a watch list, 14 of them in the Back Forty.
table_query: python -m tasks.a12_floor_screen -> a12_floor_screen (actual vs M6-expected expected win per available hour)
result: Underperformers' combined shortfall $19,423 of expected win over Jan-Jun; ratio spread (sd) 0.040
